_methodology: Hand-curated, and the file in this repo most likely to be out of date: airspace opens and closes on a timescale of weeks. Restricted airspace lengthens a flight rather than cancelling it — an aircraft routes around — so each zone carries a `detourFactor` applied to any leg whose great circle would have crossed it, not a block. The factors are estimates of how much further the diversion runs on a typical affected leg; a single number per zone is a simplification, since the real penalty depends on where the leg clips the airspace. `closedToCountries` marks a reciprocal ban, which turns on the operator's nationality rather than on the corridor: Russian airspace is closed to Western carriers and entirely open to Chinese, Gulf and Turkish ones, so an Emirati flight over Siberia is correct where a German one detours. Operator nationality isn't modelled, so the countries at the ends of the leg stand in for it. Security scores split the two cases: a reciprocal ban is a political fact and no danger to the aircraft, so those score 100 and leave the route's security untouched, while a war zone scores low. Outlines are not stored here — see AirspaceZone in engine/types.ts. Driving this from NOTAMs looks obvious and was investigated: the FAA search site is edge-blocked, its API sits behind per-application credentials on a separate portal, coverage is US-centric where the closures that matter are issued by Russian, Libyan, Sudanese and Syrian authorities, and a NOTAM is abbreviated prose with no field for 'closed to Western operators but open to Gulf ones'. Reviewing these nine zones by hand every month or two is the realistic maintenance model.
